track.title: Bayat-e Esfahan
track.notes: Tagged title: Esfahan. Same performance as 'The Masters of Persian Traditional Music, Sehtar' (1991) track 4; that transfer runs 0.75% slower (onset alignment), about 13 cents lower if the speed carries the pitch.

just_intervals.note: measured octave minus 1200 ¢, register to register

progression.narrative: The performance opens on B4 and dwells most on B in Phrase 1. Phrase 2 (0:12.4) introduces As, centred on B. Phrase 7 (2:20.1) introduces Dk, E, centred on Dk. Phrase 12 (3:23.2) introduces Db, centred on B. Phrase 15 (3:55.5) introduces Ds, centred on Ds. The line peaks at Db5 (547.2 Hz) at 4:39.7. It closes on the tonic (B2 → Dk4 → B3 → B2 → B3 → B4).

theory_fit.name: 12-tone equal temperament
theory_fit.description: Reference only: distance from the semitone grid.

theory_fit.name: Vaziri 24-tone equal temperament
theory_fit.description: Quarter-tone grid (koron/sori = exactly 50 ¢ from the natural note).

theory_fit.name: Pythagorean / Safi al-Din
theory_fit.description: Nearest note of the 17-note gamut generated by pure fifths (±8) from the tonic.

theory_fit.name: Farhat interval classes
theory_fit.description: Interval classes Hormoz Farhat measured in performance practice ("The Dastgah Concept in Persian Music", 1990). Approximate centres.

flags: tonic B set in the catalog (Bayat-e Esfahan's finalis, about B -44 cents (240.8 Hz): the pitch set fits Bayat-e Esfahan from it, and the other transfer of this performance (Masters, 1991) voted the same note. The vote picked the 2nd below, which is koron in the authentic form (Farhat 1990, p. 77). Inference, not yet by ear); the runs' vote favoured 452.4 Hz (A)
